subject.title: Workspaces: add scoped Teams control hub

question: Should OpenClaw core adopt this gateway-local multi-human Teams trust model and expose its host-bound resource authorization primitives as a permanent public plugin API?
rationale: The patch changes who may authenticate to the Gateway, how devices are approved, which persistent identities and grants core owns, and what external plugins may rely on; tests cannot decide whether that is the intended long-term security and product boundary.

options.title: Approve and stage the model
options.body: Sponsor the core direction, settle the public API contract, and split landing into bounded authorization, plugin, Workspaces, and portal stages with upgrade and live security proof.

options.title: Keep the single-owner boundary
options.body: Do not add local multi-human authentication to core and redesign sharing behind an external service or a narrower existing-owner-mediated plugin boundary.

options.title: Pause for a focused RFC
options.body: Keep the implementation open but stop merge work until maintainers document identity ownership, threat model, migration policy, and API stability expectations.

recommendation.title: Approve and stage the model
recommendation.body: Sponsor the core direction, settle the public API contract, and split landing into bounded authorization, plugin, Workspaces, and portal stages with upgrade and live security proof.

likelyOwner.reason: This person owns the current implementation and the surrounding merged Workspaces history, making them the best available technical owner to prepare the decision packet, though final approval requires repository maintainers.
